rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation affects Bs[row][33] loading when global_col=5921=N. These values are used only for computing output column = block_col*TILE_N + col_in_tile + n = 46*128 + 32 + 1 = 5921. Output write has guard 'col < N' (5921 < 5921 = false), so corrupted accum values are computed but never written.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary condition from 'global_col < N' to 'global_col <= N', which only affects the case when global_col equals exactly N=5921. This occurs in the last tile column (block_col=46) when col=33 in the Bs loading loop. The corrupted Bs[row][33] values are only used by threads computing col_in_tile=32, n=1, which produces output column 5921. However, the output write section has guard 'col < N', preventing any writes to column 5921. Thus the infection cannot propagate to observable output.
rounds.kill_strategy: The mutant is unkillable because the corrupted data path is always filtered out by the output bounds check. The mutation only affects intermediate computations for output positions that are never written.
rounds.recommendations: When designing tiled GPU kernels, ensure mutation testing considers the interaction between loading bounds checks and output bounds checks. Mutations to loading conditions may appear dangerous but can be masked by output guards that filter the same boundary cases.
